Held FLAT: SBC-zero market, no SBC charge and no dilution; the company is a net repurchaser (JPY17.3bn FY0, JPY12.8bn in Q1).
inputs.debt_basis: Bonds and borrowings only: 383,778 current + 438,184 non-current at 30-Jun-2026. The filing's 'interest-bearing debt' of 876.4bn includes ~54.4bn of lease liabilities, excluded here under lease treatment (B).
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY0 = reported FCF 75,241 (OCF 213,000 - capex 137,759) less 9,796 lease principal (treatment B); SBC 0 and interest income 0, see notes.
inputs.sbc_source: unavailable: no share-based payment line in the IFRS cash-flow statement or notes; Japanese large-cap with director-only restricted stock. Treated as an SBC-zero market (rows kept explicit at 0%), not as a missing adjustment; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fy0_note: Repo end-year label: FY2026 = year ended 31 March 2026, which the company calls FY2025. Year 1 of the projection is the company's FY2026 (ending March 2027), the guidance year.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY: 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct-2026), JPY ERP 6.0%, beta 1.2 -> cost of equity 8.9%; pre-tax cost of debt ~1.0% (interest paid 8.4bn on ~820bn of bonds and borrowings), 0.7% after tax; capital weights ~60/40 on market cap 754bn vs net debt ~745bn incl. Ultradent and a 0.8x net D/E policy ceiling -> textbook WACC ~5.6%. House uses 7.0%: the single, stated premium for an eleven-year record of ROIC below the company's own ~10% cost-of-capital estimate and the aging B&GM asset base. Risk is charged once: the same 7.0% is used in all three scenarios and cyclicality lives in the flows.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: lease principal (9,796 FY0) plus lease interest (~0.7bn) deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path (0.55% of revenue), lease liabilities (~54.4bn) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (IFRS D&A 104,744 less ~10bn RoU) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at JPY140bn (12x the FY2025-26 average profit attributable to NCI of 11.5bn; book value 124.4bn at 30-Jun-2026). FY0 NOPAT check: OI 73.8bn x (1-31%) = 50.9bn vs reported total net income 46.9bn, the gap being net finance cost.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping at year 5). Operating company, non-US cyclical -> owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations file. Equity-method profit (17.2bn FY0) sits INSIDE operating income, so affiliates are in the EBITDA flows and their investments are not in the bridge; cross-shareholdings and other non-current financial assets (100.6bn) ARE in the bridge because their dividend/interest income is in finance income, outside the flows (matching-asset rule). Ultradent (USD900m, closed 14-Aug-2026) is after the June balance sheet: added as a 139.5bn debt-equivalent in the bridge while its revenue is inside the FY2027 guidance base. EBITDA path is statutory (after special items, post-IFRS-16) because restructuring charges have recurred every year of the IFRS history (26bn FY0, 23bn prior). Price is the 30-Oct-2026 Tokyo regular close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case years 2-3 revenue growth (post guidance year); equity 5y CAGR of 7.3% is inflated by yen-weakness translation gains in OCI and is not an earnings growth rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 7.3% vs EPS 5y CAGR -9.3%: book has compounded through FX translation reserves and retained reinvestment while earnings per share fell; growth rate NOT taken from equity.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the CSV end-year labels: FY2021 (YE Mar-2021) -> FY2026 (YE Mar-2026) for 5y, FY2023 -> FY2026 for 3y. Owner FCF = OCF - capex - lease principal (SBC-zero, no interest-income strip): FY2021 89.6bn -> FY2026 65.4bn; the 3y figure is undefined because FY2023 owner FCF was -33.4bn. Cumulative owner FCF over the five IFRS years is ~72bn (~14bn/yr) on 1.6-1.9tn of revenue: the group has reinvested essentially all of its operating cash, which is why the forward path below (60-80bn mature owner FCF) is a recovery assumption, not a trend.

base.narrative: Year 1 = FY2026 guidance (revenue 1,900bn, statutory OI 83bn + D&A ~110bn -> ~10.2-10.5% EBITDA margin; capex 134bn = 7.1%). Growth then settles to 2.5-3% (specialty volume plus pass-through) fading to 1.5%. Margin recovers to 12.0% by year 5 as B&GM restructuring (polyolefin integration FY2026, Chiba ethylene FY2027) narrows the segment loss and the specialty mix rises, held there: that is between the IFRS-era statutory average (11.5%) and the pre-special-items average (~12.7%). Capex glides from 7.1% to 6.3% (~1.1x D&A) as the VISION 2030 investment phase matures. Working capital: CCC ~130 days; -15% of the revenue change credits the targeted ~10-day CCC reduction. Cash tax 31% (FY0 effective 31.6%).

bull.narrative: Specialty domains compound at the VISION 2030 pace for a few years (Ultradent plus Kulzer become a real third pillar, ICT rides semiconductor content, elastomer capacity fills), B&GM is consolidated or split off by FY2027-28 so the structural loss disappears, and a 13.5% statutory margin (still below the 14.4% FY2022 peak and well short of the FY2030 plan's ~17% implied) is sustained. Capex falls toward D&A as the asset-light strategy delivers; CCC improves.

bear.narrative: Guidance is missed as naphtha retreats and inventory gains reverse; the Chinese ethylene/polyolefin wave (5-8mt/yr through 2028) keeps B&GM loss-making and the consolidation slips; the Middle East cost hit (~5-6bn/quarter) persists; specialty growth stalls at the FY2023-26 pace and Ultradent integration drags. Margin stays at the FY2024-25 level (9.5-9.8%), capex cannot fall below 7% because plant aging (30+ years, 106 incidents FY2020-25) forces maintenance spend. Owner FCF stays near the five-year average of ~14bn/yr.

scenario_narratives.base: Mitsui Chemicals' valuation turns on two axes: whether the specialty domains (Life & Healthcare, Mobility, ICT) grow operating income faster than the FY2016-25 pace of ~6%/yr after the Ultradent and Kulzer acquisitions, and whether the Basic & Green Materials petrochemical loss (-18.4bn FY0) is removed by the FY2026-30 consolidation and split-off program. The base case delivers the FY2026 guidance year, then a gradual recovery to a 12% statutory EBITDA margin and capex gliding toward D&A, producing 60-80bn of owner FCF by the back half of the decade against a five-year history averaging ~14bn.
scenario_narratives.bull: VISION 2030 partially delivered: specialty profit compounds at high single digits, B&GM is separated by FY2027-28, margin reaches 13.5%, capex falls to ~1.07x D&A, working capital is released, and the terminal multiple rises to 15x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: Petrochemical oversupply, naphtha and FX volatility, and a slow specialty ramp keep the group at its FY2024-25 margin with capex stuck at 7% of revenue; owner FCF stays near the historical average, the terminal value is small (12x) and the equity is left with the debt, NCI and Ultradent claims ahead of it.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: B&GM is structurally loss-making against a multi-year Chinese capacity wave, management has conceded that specialty growth lags its own plan, and the five-year owner-FCF record is roughly zero. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: specialty acceleration, a B&GM separation that has not been decided, and the integration of two large dental acquisitions.

valuation_philosophy.summary: An owner-FCF view of a capital-intensive Japanese chemical group. The market prices the stock at ~0.86x book and ~8x EV/EBITDA on a restructuring and re-rating thesis; the cash-flow model values what the assets actually return after capex, working capital, leases, minorities and the Ultradent payment. The gap between the two is the price of the VISION 2030 thesis stated explicitly. Terminal values are capped at 12-15x owner FCF (cyclical), which corresponds to roughly 4-5x EBITDA, below the group's own trading history, so the model carries no re-rating.
key_risks_to_valuation: Owner FCF has averaged ~14bn/yr over the five IFRS years; any mature-state FCF assumption is a recovery call, and the DCF is very sensitive to the capex-to-D&A convergence.
Working-capital capture at -15% of the revenue change on a ~130-day CCC: a naphtha-driven revenue jump consumes cash in year 1.
The NCI deduction (140bn) and the Ultradent bridge (139.5bn at JPY155/USD) are each ~JPY390/share; the FX rate on Ultradent and the NCI multiple are judgment calls.
Statutory EBITDA includes recurring restructuring charges (~1.5% of revenue); if the B&GM program ends them, the base margin path is conservative by that amount.
Terminal cap multiples (12-15x FCF) bind in every scenario; the Gordon value at 7%/1.5% would be ~18.5x.
